archetype.name: Retooling (top-heavy)
archetype.definition: A team whose elite forwards and special teams keep games close while the 5-on-5 structure, and the blueline above all, is still the one that sank last season.

report.headline: A perfect penalty kill is hiding the same 5-on-5 problem as last year
report.take:
Toronto is 3-4-2 and 21st on the site, one year after a 78-point season that ranked 29th. The forward group earns its B. Auston Matthews sits first of 220 centers with 13 points, and Nylander, Marchenko and rookie Easton Cowan give the top nine real finishing. The blueline earns its D-. Six listed defensemen have zero goals between them, Jake McCabe has no points in nearly 20 minutes a night and ranks 215th of 242, and the team bleeds 29.2 shots against a game, 26th in the league.

The record is being held together by special teams. The power play converts 26.7% (7th), which a group with Matthews, Marchenko and Tavares each at four PP points can plausibly keep up. The penalty kill is at 96.4% against a league average of 79%, which is not a skill level anyone sustains. At 5-on-5 the Leafs get 44.4% of the expected goals (28th) and 46% of the attempts (24th). That is almost exactly last season's 45.6% xGF, so the team that finished near the bottom has not changed underneath.

The numbers do hide some bad luck. The 5-on-5 PDO of 96.5 means even-strength results have been worse than the chances, and Pts vs Goal Diff of -1.1 (27th) says three one-goal or overtime losses cost them points. The all-situations PDO of 100.1 is ordinary only because the kill is propping it up. When the PK comes back to earth, the 5-on-5 luck has to swing up just to keep the record where it is.

The direction is roughly flat. The last five games went 2-2-1 with 18 goals each way, exactly the season's points rate. The pace of 73 points would be close to a repeat of last year. Matthews keeps them watchable and in most games, but without better defense they look like a bubble-to-lottery team rather than a playoff one.

strengths.title: Matthews leads a deep scoring top nine
strengths.body: Matthews is the top-ranked center on the site and drives play as well as scores, with a 53.8% xGF. Marchenko (58.3%) and Cowan (60.4%) are winning their minutes, and the forwards have 28 of the team's goals. This is the most sustainable part of the roster.

strengths.title: A power play with real weapons
strengths.body: At 26.7%, well above the league's 20.4%, the power play is doing a lot of the scoring. Four different forwards have three or four PP points, so it is not riding one hot shooter. Expect some cooling, but it should stay above average.

concerns.title: Outplayed at 5-on-5, again
concerns.body: A 44.4% xGF ranks 28th, and last season's 45.6% shows this is a pattern rather than a slump. Opponents get more shots than Toronto does, and the gap is widest in shots against. Nylander (38%), McKenna (36.8%) and Tavares (30%) are being caved in when they're on the ice.

concerns.title: A blueline with nothing to give
concerns.body: The D- grade is earned. The defense has produced zero goals and 10 assists, the top-pairing minutes go to a 100th-ranked Raddysh, and McCabe is pointless. That leaves the forwards to create everything and the goalies to clean up the volume.

concerns.title: The penalty kill will regress hard
concerns.body: A 96.4% kill is 17 points above the league average. It is the biggest reason the all-situations numbers look ordinary. When it settles toward normal, a team already allowing above-average goals will allow more.

trend.note: The record has not moved in either direction: the last five games matched the season's points rate. Both scoring and goals allowed ran a bit higher lately, so the games are getting looser rather than better.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, two soft goalie matchups, one wall in New York
weekAhead.body:
Calgary and Columbus are the chances to bank points. Calgary has the league's worst save percentage and worst GSAx, and Columbus kills only 68% of penalties, so Toronto's power play has openings in both. Edmonton is the opposite case. The Oilers are 6-1-1 on a league-best 19.2% shooting and a 108.7 all-situations PDO, which won't last, but their 70.8% kill invites the Leafs' power play.

The Rangers at home are the hard one. Their A+ goaltending is stopping 92.7%, and they have held wingers to the fewest points relative to expectation in the league. A low-scoring game there plays to Toronto's leaky defense only if Bobrovsky matches Shesterkin-level goaltending. A split of four, with points in Calgary and Columbus, is the realistic target.

keyMatchups.title: Matthews against Calgary's porous middle
keyMatchups.body: Calgary allows centers almost a full point a game above their norms, 31st in the league, behind an F-grade goaltending group. If Matthews and Roslovic don't fill the net in Calgary, it says something about Toronto rather than the matchup.

keyMatchups.title: Power play versus weak kills
keyMatchups.body: Columbus and Edmonton both kill penalties far below the league average. Toronto's 7th-ranked power play is the most direct path to goals on the road trip.

keyMatchups.title: Nylander's wing against the Rangers
keyMatchups.body: New York ranks first at suppressing wingers. Nylander's 38% xGF suggests he is already living on finishing rather than possession, which makes this the hardest night of the week for him.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the penalty kill finally gives some goals back, and whether 5-on-5 play improves enough to cover it.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the power play to stay strong and Matthews to stay elite. Expect the penalty kill to fall toward the league norm, which will push goals against up from an already below-average level. Some 5-on-5 bounce-back is due given a 96.5 PDO and a -1.1 Pts vs Goal Diff, and that should roughly offset the PK regression. That leaves the season near its 73-point pace, with upside only if the blueline gets help or the xGF climbs toward 48%.

This looks like a team between 74 and 86 points: better than last year at the edges, not a playoff team in an Atlantic where five clubs already have winning records.
swingFactors: How far the penalty kill regresses
Bobrovsky holding a save % near .890 or better

confidence.note: Nine games is small, but the 5-on-5 numbers match last season.
